titulo: Module 03 — Exam: structured output, validation with retry, and the Batch API

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: a pipeline asks the model to 'respond only with JSON' and parses the response. On 4% of documents the parse fails because there is text before the JSON or a field is missing. What is the BEST fix?
opcoes: Use structured outputs (output_config.format with the extraction's JSON schema)
Extract the JSON with a regex that looks for the first '{' and the last '}'
Repeat the instruction 'ONLY JSON' at the beginning and at the end of the prompt
Prefill the assistant turn with '{'
questoes.explicacao: Structured outputs guarantees a response that conforms to the schema; the other options are patches or are invalid on newer models.
feedbacks: Correct.
A fragile patch: it handles the surrounding text, not the missing field.
Emphasis gives no structural guarantee.
Prefill returns 400 on newer models and doesn't guarantee the schema.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: the extractor used a record_invoice tool with tool_choice: {type: tool, name: record_invoice} only to get JSON. After migrating to a newer model, every call returns 400. What should be done?
opcoes: Switch to tool_choice: {type: any}
Revert to the previous model
Use structured outputs with the same schema
Remove the schema and validate the text with try/catch, repeating the call if it fails
questoes.explicacao: On newer models, forced any/tool returns 400; when forcing existed only to get JSON, structured outputs is the replacement.
feedbacks: any is also forced and also returns 400.
Avoids the problem without solving it; there is a direct replacement.
Correct.
Loses the structural guarantee.

questoes.pergunta: Customer Support scenario: the agent calls create_ticket in a tool loop. Sometimes it sends extra fields, or sends the priority field as a free-form string instead of one of the accepted values, and the backend rejects it. What is the BEST fix?
opcoes: Validate in the backend and return 'Operation failed' to the model
Enable strict: true on the tool, with an enum on priority and additionalProperties: false
Replace the tool with structured outputs on the final response
Add a list of the allowed fields to the prompt
questoes.explicacao: In a tool loop, strict guarantees arguments that follow the schema exactly.
feedbacks: A generic error (anti-pattern), and it doesn't prevent the problem.
Correct.
Structured outputs formats the response, not the arguments of an action in the middle of the loop.
The prompt helps, but it doesn't guarantee anything.

questoes.pergunta: A dev turned on strict: true for a tool whose schema has 5 properties, only 3 of them in required, and doesn't declare additionalProperties. The data for 2 of those properties sometimes doesn't exist in the source. Which adjustment is the most appropriate?
opcoes: None: strict infers the rest
Remove required from all properties, so that strict treats everything as optional
Add minimum/maximum to the numeric fields
Declare additionalProperties: false and, preferably, put everything in required, with nullable where data may be missing
questoes.explicacao: additionalProperties: false is mandatory for strict. Optional properties are allowed (they count toward a limit), but required + nullable makes the absence explicit.
feedbacks: Strict doesn't infer anything; additionalProperties: false is mandatory.
It doesn't address the missing requirement, and it multiplies optional properties, which count toward a limit and leave the absence ambiguous.
Numeric constraints aren't supported by strict (400 on the raw schema).
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: with strict enabled, 100% of the invoices validate against the schema. The audit found 2% with a total that differs from the sum of the line items. What is the BEST action?
opcoes: Add a description to the schema: 'the total must be the sum of the items'
Replace strict with structured outputs
Validate the sum in code and resend with the specific error (values and suspect item)
Accept it, since the schema validated
questoes.explicacao: Schema ≠ semantics: business rules are validated in code and feed the retry.
feedbacks: A description in the schema is only guidance; it doesn't guarantee the rule.
Both guarantee format, not semantics.
Correct.
Confuses conformance with correctness.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: many invoices don't include the purchase order number. The schema has purchase_order as a required string, and the model fills in plausible made-up values. What is the fix?
opcoes: Make purchase_order nullable (few-shot: missing = null)
Remove the field from the schema
Add a retry until the field comes back filled in, with a limit of 3 attempts
Instruct the model to 'not make things up'
questoes.explicacao: A required, non-nullable field forces the model to invent; nullable allows the honest output.
feedbacks: Correct.
Loses the data when it does exist.
Retry doesn't create missing data; it reinforces the fabrication.
An instruction doesn't remove the pressure from the schema.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: the contract_type field has enum [purchase, sale, lease]. Loan-for-use (commodatum) contracts are coming out as 'lease', distorting reports. What adjustment?
opcoes: Add 'unclear' to the enum
Remove the enum and accept free text
Add few-shot with lease examples so the model learns the boundary
Add 'other' to the enum + a nullable detail field
questoes.explicacao: 'other' + detail avoids forcing a wrong category and preserves the information.
feedbacks: 'unclear' is for an ambiguous source; a loan-for-use contract is clear, it just isn't on the list.
Loses standardization and the structural guarantee.
Lease examples don't teach where to put loan-for-use contracts.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: on poor scans, it's impossible to tell whether the contract was signed. The signed field is a boolean, and in those cases the model answers true or false at random. What is the best way to model it?
opcoes: Keep the boolean and ask the model to be conservative
Use an enum [signed, not_signed, unclear]
Make the field a free-form string
Remove the field and manually check every contract
questoes.explicacao: 'unclear' avoids guessing when the source doesn't allow a decision, and lets you route those cases to review.
feedbacks: Vague; it still forces a binary guess.
Correct.
Loses structure and standardization.
Disproportionate: only the illegible ones need review.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: the team turned on strict for a tool whose schema defines quantity with minimum: 1 and zip_code with maxLength: 9. The requests started returning 400. What is the BEST action?
opcoes: Turn off strict, since it's incompatible with the schema
Open a ticket: it's an API bug
Remove those constraints from the schema (or let the SDK helper move them into the description) and validate them in code
Replace the tool with an assistant prefill containing the partial JSON
questoes.explicacao: minimum and maxLength aren't supported by strict: in the raw schema they return 400. Remove them from the schema (SDK helpers do this and validate locally) and enforce the rule in your code.
feedbacks: Loses the format guarantee just to keep constraints the API wouldn't even enforce.
Documented behavior: an unsupported feature in a raw schema returns 400.
Correct.
Prefill returns 400 on newer models and doesn't guarantee the schema.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: the retry loop sends 'The extraction failed validation. Try again.' and the correction rate on the 2nd attempt is only 10%. What is the BEST improvement?
opcoes: Increase the number of attempts to 5
Include the specific errors (field, rule, values)
Switch to a larger model only on retries, keeping the smaller one on the first attempt
Increase effort only on retries
questoes.explicacao: Specific errors tell the model what to fix and where; a generic message produces the same response.
feedbacks: More attempts without information repeat the error.
Correct.
More expensive, without addressing the lack of information in the feedback.
More reasoning without knowing what's wrong helps little.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: the delivery_date field fails validation (it is required by the business). After 3 retries with a specific error, it is still empty or made up. Analysis shows that these documents simply don't state the date. What should be done?
opcoes: Accept null in the field and route the document to the human review queue
Raise the retry limit to 10
Fill it in with the issue date as a default
Instruct the model to estimate the date based on the usual lead time
questoes.explicacao: Retry doesn't recover information missing from the source; the honest answer is null and, if the business requires it, review.
feedbacks: Correct.
More retries, same absence: it only increases cost and the chance of fabrication.
Fabricated data that looks genuine.
Explicitly induces hallucination.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: during a peak, a corrupted document stayed in a retry loop for hours, generating a high cost. The code only exits the loop when validation passes. What is the correct design?
opcoes: Remove validation for corrupted documents
Increase the API timeout
Save the last result, even if invalid, after 1 hour, marking it as 'pending'
Cap the attempts and, once they are exhausted, fail explicitly
questoes.explicacao: The cap is a backstop; once it is exhausted, fail explicitly, never saving invalid data or silently discarding it.
feedbacks: Lets invalid data through.
Doesn't solve the endless loop.
Saves invalid data as if it were good.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: CI scenario: a security scanner built on Claude produces findings that the devs frequently dismiss. The team wants to know which kinds of patterns produce useful findings and which get dismissed, in order to refine the prompt. Which output change helps?
opcoes: Add a confidence field from 0 to 100 and automatically discard findings below 60
Generate a free-text report at the end
A detected_pattern field on each finding, measured per pattern
Reduce the number of findings per PR
questoes.explicacao: detected_pattern lets you measure per pattern and refine or turn off the noisy ones.
feedbacks: Self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated and doesn't identify the pattern.
Free text isn't measurable.
Correct.
Cuts without knowing what is noise.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: the audit team wants to identify invoices in which the printed total diverges from the line items (a supplier error). Today the model extracts only total and sometimes 'corrects' the value on its own. What is the best way to model it?
opcoes: Extract declared_total and computed_items_sum, and compare them in code
Instruct the model to always recalculate the total
Extract only the items and calculate the total in code, ignoring the printed one
Ask the model for a boolean field 'looks_correct'
questoes.explicacao: Declared + computed exposes the discrepancy instead of hiding it.
feedbacks: Correct.
Hides the discrepancy the audit wants to find.
Loses the declared value; there is no way to detect the discrepancy.
An opaque, unverifiable judgment.

questoes.pergunta: CI scenario: the automated PR review is expensive. An engineer proposes sending the reviews through the Batch API to save 50%. The review is a required check before merge. What is the assessment?
opcoes: Good idea: 50% savings with no loss of quality
Inappropriate for the gate (up to 24h, no SLA); suitable for a nightly sweep
Good idea, as long as the batch has only one request per PR
Inappropriate because the Batch API doesn't support structured output in batch requests
questoes.explicacao: Batch has no SLA and can take up to 24h; it isn't suitable for a blocking step.
feedbacks: Ignores latency: the PR would sit blocked for hours.
Correct.
Batch size doesn't create an SLA.
The reason is wrong: batch works with structured output; the problem is latency.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: the company needs to extract 50,000 historical contracts by the end of the week. The prompt was written yesterday and hasn't been tested on real documents yet. What is the most appropriate plan?
opcoes: Send all 50,000 to the batch now, to save time
Process all 50,000 synchronously, in parallel
Send 50 batches of 1,000 and fix the prompt between them as errors show up
Refine the prompt on a synchronous sample, then run the volume through batch
questoes.explicacao: Refine on a sample before the volume; after that, batch is ideal (no minute-level urgency, 50% cheaper).
feedbacks: Risks paying for 50,000 extractions with a flawed prompt.
Pays double with no need for real time.
Uses the volume as a lab: slow and expensive.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: in a nightly batch, the prompt lets the model call the lookup_supplier tool to enrich the extraction. Many results come back incomplete, ending in a tool_use with no response. What is the cause and the fix?
opcoes: A timeout bug; increase max_tokens
Batch doesn't run a multi-turn tool loop; put the data in the request or go synchronous
strict: true was missing on the lookup_supplier tool, so the arguments came out invalid and the call was aborted
The custom_id values are duplicated
questoes.explicacao: Each batch request is a single call; nobody returns the tool_result inside the batch.
feedbacks: It isn't truncation: the stop_reason would be tool_use.
Correct.
strict validates arguments; it doesn't create the loop that batch lacks.
Duplicate custom_id values don't explain a tool_use with no response.

questoes.pergunta: Regarding structured output, which TWO statements are correct? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Conformance to the schema doesn't guarantee that the values are semantically correct
With strict: true, minimum and maxLength become guaranteed by the API
The top-level output_format parameter is the recommended path for structured outputs
To use strict, every object in the schema needs additionalProperties: false
A closed enum without 'other' is the best way to avoid wrong classifications
questoes.explicacao: Schema ≠ semantics; strict requires additionalProperties: false on every object.
feedbacks: Correct.
Numeric and length constraints aren't supported by strict (400 on the raw schema).
Top-level output_format is deprecated; use output_config.format.
Correct.
A closed enum forces a wrong choice when the category isn't on the list.

questoes.pergunta: You are designing an extractor's validation loop. Which TWO practices are correct? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Repeat until validation passes, with no limit
Use the same generic message on every retry so as not to bias the model
Validate the schema and also semantic rules (sums, impossible dates, contradictions between fields)
Keep retrying when the required field doesn't exist in the source
When the limit is exhausted, fail explicitly and route to review
questoes.explicacao: Validate form and meaning; use a cap as a backstop and fail explicitly at the end.
feedbacks: A loop with no limit: uncontrolled cost.
A generic message doesn't say what to fix.
Correct.
Retry doesn't recover missing information.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: A team runs its weekly report extraction through the Batch API. Which TWO practices are correct? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Read the results as soon as the batch is created, in the order of the input file
Poll processing_status until ended and match each result by its custom_id
On seeing a few errored results, resubmit the entire batch
Also use the batch for the managers' real-time query dashboard
Resubmit only the custom_id values with an errored or expired result
questoes.explicacao: Poll until ended, match by custom_id, and resubmit only what failed.
feedbacks: Results are ready only at the end, and they arrive out of order.
Correct.
Reprocesses successes and doubles the cost unnecessarily.
Real time doesn't fit with batch (up to 24h, no SLA).
Correct.
